key_insight: DrugGen-2 is a disease-aware generative language model that improves small-molecule design by conditioning on both disease ontology and target protein sequence.
engineering_relevance: It shows how adding disease context to molecular generation can improve candidate quality for AI-driven drug discovery and repurposing pipelines.
method: Fine-tunes a pretrained GPT-2 model on approved drug–disease–target data
Uses supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO reinforcement learning
Rewards validity, novelty, diversity, and predicted binding affinity
evidence_signal: On five diabetic nephropathy-related protein targets, DrugGen-2 outperformed DrugGPT and DrugGen, with stronger uniqueness, better similarity to approved drugs, and improved predicted affinities; docking identified candidates with affinities as low as -9.917.
watch_item: Reported gains rely on predicted affinity and docking rather than experimental validation, so real-world biological efficacy and safety remain unconfirmed.
paper_title: DrugGen 2: A disease-aware language model for enhancing drug discovery
